questions.rationale: Too many low-value alerts can desensitise users and increase override behaviour.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A barcode system confirms the medicine, but the patient says it is not their usual dose. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Ask the patient to accept it.
Pause and verify the order, patient and clinical context.

questions.rationale: Technology supports but does not replace clinical judgement or patient participation.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A smart pump alert is overridden repeatedly because limits do not match local protocols. What is the BEST leadership response?

options.text: Review the drug library, workflow and override data with frontline users.

questions.rationale: Frequent overrides are safety signals that may reflect poor configuration or workflow mismatch.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which risk is associated with copied electronic medication orders?

options.text: Outdated or incorrect information may be carried forward.

questions.rationale: Copying can perpetuate outdated doses, weights, indications or durations.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Why should frontline nurses be involved in technology implementation?

options.text: They understand real workflow and potential workarounds.
They remove the need for testing.

questions.rationale: Clinical users can identify usability risks and workflow mismatch before and after implementation.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: What is an essential component of medication-system downtime planning?

options.text: A safe alternative process for orders, verification, administration and documentation.

questions.rationale: Downtime plans maintain safe medication processes when electronic systems are unavailable.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A patient's weight in the electronic record is outdated and drives a dose calculation. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Verify the current weight and correct the record before use.

questions.rationale: Critical input data must be accurate because technology can amplify incorrect information.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which implementation strategy best reduces unsafe workarounds?

options.text: Analyse workflow, train staff, simulate use and monitor practice.

questions.rationale: Successful implementation aligns technology with clinical work and includes testing, training and monitoring.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: How can barcode technology improve medication safety?

options.text: By strengthening patient and product identification.
By removing the need for documentation.

questions.rationale: Barcode systems support identification but do not replace professional checks.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which finding most strongly suggests poor digital-system design?

options.text: High rates of workarounds and repeated near misses.

questions.rationale: Workarounds and near misses often indicate a mismatch between technology and workflow.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A hospital shares a successful medication intervention internationally. What is the most appropriate approach?

options.text: Assume one solution fits all settings.
Adapt it to local resources, policy and practice before implementation.

questions.rationale: Global learning should be adapted to local context and resources.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which digital control best reduces infusion-programming errors?

options.text: A well-maintained smart-pump drug library with appropriate limits.

questions.rationale: Configured dose-error reduction software can support safer programming when maintained and monitored.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A clinical decision-support system recommends a dose that conflicts with renal results. What should the nurse do?

options.text: Apply clinical judgement and seek review before administration.

questions.rationale: Decision support does not replace assessment, evidence or professional accountability.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Why should override rates be monitored?

options.text: Frequent overrides may indicate alert fatigue, poor settings or unsafe practice.

questions.rationale: Override data can reveal technology and workflow risks requiring review.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which information-governance practice is correct?

options.text: Photograph medication charts on personal devices.
Access medication records only for legitimate care purposes and protect passwords.

questions.rationale: Digital convenience does not reduce confidentiality and security obligations.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A global supply alert identifies contamination in a medicine batch. What should nurse leaders do?

options.text: Verify local stock, communicate the alert and follow recall procedures.

questions.rationale: Global medication risks can affect local supply chains and require prompt coordinated action.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which outcome best indicates safe technology implementation?

options.text: Relevant errors decrease without creating excessive delays or workarounds.

questions.rationale: Implementation should improve safety while remaining usable and sustainable.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: A remote monitoring system generates many false alerts. What should leaders do?

options.text: Review thresholds, clinical workflow and response protocols with users and technical staff.

questions.rationale: Excessive false alerts create fatigue and require collaborative system optimisation.

questions.sectionLabel: Digital Medication Safety, Innovation and Global Collaboration
questions.stem: Which outcome BEST reflects the role of a Global Nursing Professional in digital medication safety?

options.text: Leave technology decisions entirely to IT.
Use technology critically, report hazards, lead improvement and preserve clinical judgement.

questions.rationale: Global professionals combine digital capability, governance, clinical judgement and system improvement.
